description.narrative:
The WASH response led by PARC with support of Oxfam will prioritize rehabilitation of existing municipal water systems over trucking, based on cost-effectiveness (1.2 EUR/m³ vs. 20-25 EUR/m³) and sustainability. This approach addresses infrastructure damage whilerestoring systems for longer-term continuity rather than perpetuating emergency modalities. Private well fuel support will provide interim solutions where public systems remain non-functional, coordinated through UNOPS/WASH Cluster mechanisms. Emergency sanitation will target HH-level latrine installation to address severe overcrowding at communal facilities. Prioritization of female-headed HHs and families with PWDs implemented in coordination with protection partners directly addresses identified gaps in access for vulnerable population. Wastewater network repairs and winterization preparedness will be implemented as distinct components, enabling targeted flood mitigation ahead of seasonal risks. HP will adopt a community-led model through trained CBVs and WASH committees, addressing limited community health mobilization while building local ownership. This combines behaviour change messaging with NFI provision, recognizing that affordability barriers require both supply and demand-side interventions. Hygiene kits will be provided through Unicef/IOM pipeline while MHM vouchers through vetted vendors will address dignity needs while supporting local markets. InfectionPrevention and outbreak risk mitigation will be addressed through strengthened WASH service delivery and hygiene promotion in line with WASH Cluster guidance. Solid waste management will focus on time-bound emergency collection services and community clean-up activities coordinated through the WASH Cluster/SWM Taskforce including the JSC to reduce environmental contamination and public healthrisks.
FS <(>&<)> Livelihoods response led by PARC and Oxfam address the "liquidity and infrastructure trap" constraining agricultural recovery through complementary interventions targeting both the water bottleneck and income gap. Planned interventions under Result 3 are structured across two complementary activities. Activity 3.1 addresses the water infrastructure bottleneck through the rehabilitation of three partially damaged agricultural wells (covering essential mechanical and electrical repairs) and the installation of approximately 4 km of primary and secondary irrigation lines, alongside fuel subsidization for six operational and rehabilitated wells over three months. Well rehabilitation will be implemented through direct technical supervision by PARC field engineers, supported by qualified local technicians contracted through a competitive process; irrigation line installation will follow the same subcontracting modality, ensuring quality control and accountability throughout. Activity 3.2 addresses the income and input gap through voucher-based emergency livelihood support to 60 small-scale farmers, enabling direct procurement of priority agricultural inputs from pre-qualified local vendors under framework agreements. Implementation of both activities is carried out jointly by Oxfam andPARC, with overall coordination maintained through the MoA, the Food Security Cluster, and the Agriculture Working Group.

participating-org.narrative: In 1983 a small group of agronomists founded the Palestinian Agricultural Relief Committees (PARC), which has since developed into one of the most important Palestinian non-governmental organisations providing services to poor and marginalised farmers onthe West Bank and Gaza Strip, working to make agricultural businesses grow. PARC#s goal is to promote an economic and social climate that would allow the Palestinian agricultural sector to develop sustainably. Another goal is to improve the living standard of Palestinians living in rural areas, especially of poor farming families. PARC provides a broad range of agricultural extension services. It is active in land reclamation and in building rural access roads. The organisation advocates the improvementof rural women#s economic position. It is part of an Oxfam Novib-funded three-year gender-focus program. In 1991 PARC got an ISO-certification. It was the first and so far only non-governmental organisation in the Arab world to obtain one. It has also developed an impressive strategic ten-year plan for the 1998-2008 period. Together with several other agricultural non-governmental organisations (NGOs) PARC has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Agriculture, which sees PARC#s workasindependent and complementary to its own. PARC is active in a network of Palestinian NGOs and a member of the governing committee of the Palestinian NGO-network. Oxfam Novib has been supporting PARC since 1982. In 1999 Oxfam Novib, ICCO, Christian Aid (UK) and Oxfam Great Britain set up a donor consortium to support PARC. This provides PARC a measure of long-term financial security. It also makes technical and organisational assistance available to PARC in further developing its program.
